ledger.claim: The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry the same trip_id, TRP-00719, and the same start instant (the trip_record's started_at of 2026-09-27T11:18:40 is the gps_trace's first_fix_at to the second), so the artifacts describe one and the same trip and the rider's first burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged.

This trip has an amended dropoff, and that is a stored fact and not a hypothesis: the trip_record's dropoff_amended_at is 2026-09-27T11:27:40, the booked 'Original back-gate pin' (1.328, 103.84678) was replaced by 'Central Gardens destination' (1.328, 103.8475), and the chat log carries the same exchange between 11:26:50 and 11:27:45. POL-RD-05 is therefore engaged on this trip.

The amendment timestamp is present but the re-quote behind it is not: amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null on the trip_record. POL-RD-05 says in terms that the clause cannot then be run, that no substitute figure may be derived, and that POL-RD-10(5) applies. What would resolve it is the amended optimal distance and duration stored at re-quote, and nothing in this bundle supplies them.

Because the amended route estimate is missing, the record cannot answer the only question the rider actually raises - whether the move from the pre-amendment quote of 13.80 to the charged 22.40 was justified. POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory in that state rather than discretionary, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected or refunded, so the rider is not left carrying the disputed 8.60 while a human reads the re-quote.

The rider does not allege extra kilometres and none exist: the trace governs the measurement under POL-RD-01 and records 10.99 km against an optimal route of 11 km, an excess of -0.01 km, so the driver took no longer route. That locates the disputed 8.60 precisely - it is not a distance charge - and on this UPFRONT_QUOTE trip POL-RD-11 closes the distance-and-time refund route, leaving the rider's whole case resting on the re-quote that followed the pin move, which is the very figure the bundle omits.

The driver's account that 'the rider edited the destination herself' is not the whole record: the chat log shows the driver writing at 11:26:50 'Just move the pin to Block B, same price' and the rider replying at 11:27:45 'I changed it and the app now says 22.40, not 13.80'. The driver's own message corroborates the rider's account that she moved the pin on the representation that the price would not change; an assertion that names no evidence ID carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

To the extent the driver relies on the pin move itself to excuse the uplift, POL-RD-04 does not carry him: that clause requires the instruction to come from the rider and to be corroborated by waypoint_hint or a named road travelled, and here the instruction came from the driver and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the corroboration test is undecidable on the record and the clause is unavailable.

The trace is the governing distance measurement and it shows no deviation at all. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 10.99 km against the booked optimal of 11.0 km on the trip record, an excess of minus 0.01 km, or minus 0.09%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; both gates fail, and the clause is explicit that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The trace carrying that measurement is unimpaired and needs no corroboration. It holds 115 fixes at a 10-second cadence across the whole trip, coverage_pct 100.0, no recorded gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires: there is no gap beyond 90 seconds, no straight-line jump beyond 500 m and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The trace is therefore not impaired for policy purposes, its figure governs, and there is no route to discounting it.

This trip is priced on an upfront quote, which closes the distance-refund route entirely. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 22.40 while total_charged is 22.40, so the charge exceeds the quote by 0.00. POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront trip, and under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's only money remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quoted fare plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. That amount is nil, and the unrecovered cost of any detour falls on the driver rather than the rider.

There is no pass-through and no billing-integrity correction to make. The ledger carries no ERP gantries and tolls_erp of 0.00, an airport surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and a waiting_time_fee of 0.00; properly_chargeable totals 0.00. Every charge line has a counterpart on the trace and the trip record, so POL-RD-09(4)'s standalone billing-integrity refund - the one remedy available whether or not a deviation exists - yields nothing, and POL-RD-09(2)'s off-route ERP correction has nothing to attach to.

The rider's arithmetic depends on a 13.80 quote that exists nowhere in the ledger. fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd is 22.40, and the published line items - 3.80 base fare, 12.20 distance fare, 5.60 time fare and 0.80 platform fee - sum to exactly 22.40. Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace; the trace shows a 0.01 km shortfall rather than an excess, and no artifact in the bundle records a 13.80 fare for this trip.

The only amendment on the record is the rider's own act and cannot be converted into a charge against the driver. The chat log records her message at 11:27:45, 'I changed it and the app now says 22.40, not 13.80', and the trip record timestamps the dropoff amendment at 11:27:40, nine minutes after the trip started at 11:18:40 - the ride was already under way. POL-RD-05 provides that distance driven before the amendment timestamp is never counted as excess against the driver, and on this trace there is no excess to exclude in any event.

POL-RD-05's re-baselining is not reached, so the missing amended_optimal_distance_km leaves nothing undecided. The clause exists to strip out an excess that the amended endpoints would otherwise create; here the measured excess is negative, so there is no excess to re-base and no need for a substitute amended optimal - which the clause itself forbids anyone to derive. The driver invokes no exculpatory clause against an artifact that lacks a field the clause requires: his case is simply that POL-RD-01's gate fails on the booked optimal, evidenced by the trace. The POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger is therefore not engaged and no part of the contested amount should be held back from the ruling.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be charged against this driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, far below both the 3-flag trigger and the 0.05 ratio trigger that POL-RD-06 sets, so even if the tribunal were to consult the profile there is no pattern to establish and no basis for a FULL_REFUND uplift or a conduct referral on this trip.

NO_ACTION is the outcome the evidence supports on this rider-filed dispute. Under POL-GEN-03 that value leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they stand, which is what a claim the evidence does not support produces; it does not restore or create any charge, and it returns nothing to the rider.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case cannot be decided on the present record, so it goes to a human reviewer and the disputed SGD 8.60 is held — neither collected nor refunded — until that review is done.

What both sides agree on, and I accept. There was no route deviation. EV-GPS-00719 measures 10.99 km against the booked optimal of 11.0 km on EV-TRIP-00719, an excess of −0.01 km (−0.09%). Both POL-RD-01 gates fail (not over 20% of optimal, not over 0.8 km), so no deviation is established however the trip is characterised, and the trace backing that measurement is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (115 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s). The trip is priced UPFRONT_QUOTE (EV-FARE-00719: quoted_fare_sgd 22.40, total_charged 22.40, charged_over_quote 0.00), so POL-RD-02 does not run and POL-RD-11 leaves no distance-or-time refund; and with no ERP, no airport surcharge and no waiting fee (properly_chargeable 0.00) POL-RD-09 gives no pass-through or billing-integrity correction. The 13.80 figure the rider relies on appears in no artifact — only in her own in-app message of 11:27:45 — so I treat it as her account of what the app showed, not a ledger fare.

Why the case nonetheless cannot be closed. The dropoff was amended: the pin moved roughly 80 m (from 'Original back-gate pin', 1.328/103.84678, to 'Central Gardens destination', 1.328/103.8475), and EV-TRIP-00719 carries dropoff_amended_at 2026-09-27T11:27:40. But amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 requires the deviation test to be re-run against the route between the amended endpoints, and says in terms that where the amendment timestamp is present but that figure is missing, the re-quote is absent, the clause cannot be run, no substitute may be derived, and POL-RD-10(5) applies. POL-RD-10(5) names this exact state — 'a POL-RD-05 amendment with amended_optimal_distance_km null' — as a mandatory trigger. I therefore reject the driver's submission that POL-RD-05 is 'not reached' because the measured excess is negative: the clause is engaged by the amendment itself and its duty to re-baseline does not depend on there being a positive excess. The record is incomplete; that is a data failure, not a finding for either side. The driver's POL-RD-04 answer also fails — the pin move was requested by the driver ('Just move the pin to Block B, same price'), not the rider, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the clause's corroboration test cannot be run. No traffic cause is asserted by either side, so the MISSING advisory (EV-ADVIS-00719-01, weight 0.0) escalates nothing by itself under POL-RD-13. And with driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d 0 over 250 completed trips in 90 days, no POL-RD-06 pattern and no conduct referral arises.

What would resolve it: the amended optimal distance and duration stored when the re-quote was issued (and, if available, the pre-move quoted fare). With those, the amended-baseline deviation test can be run and the rider's fare question answered. Confidence is 0.85; the deciding artifacts (EV-TRIP-00719, EV-GPS-00719, EV-FARE-00719, EV-CHAT-00719) all carry weight 1.0, so nothing in the ruling is discounted.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
